notes: Fixture checkout (evals/fixtures/checkout) is a tiny Python checkout service with a seeded change delivered as change.patch. The patch subject claims it 'guards negative quantities', but the diff does not touch quantities or negative prices at all (verified: apply_discount(-10,10) == -9.0), the intent-parrot HARD FAIL trap. The changed apply_discount has one call site affected by the new clamp (cart.checkout_total, passes an out-of-range-capable discount_pct) and one not reached by the clamp (reports.promo_preview, fixed PREVIEW_PCT=10), the cross-file scoping test. The change adds round() money rounding whose agreement with the downstream payment processor is not derivable from the repo, the must-flag unverifiable HARD FAIL trap. test_pricing.py passes on the happy path only, so 'verified green' must come from a real run and the clamp/negative paths must be grounded as untested. unrelated.py is a scope decoy the brief must not narrate. Fixture logfix tests over-production restraint on a one-line typo fix. Score against a no-skill baseline arm (>=3 reps, >=2 model tiers) per evidence-protocol.md; the two HARD FAILs are pass^k on every rep.

evals.name: reviewer-brief-on-checkout-change
evals.prompt: I'm about to ship this change to our checkout service. Explain it for the reviewer so they can decide whether to merge. The change is in ./checkout/change.patch and the code is in ./checkout.
evals.expected_output: A terse reviewer brief grounded in the diff and a real test run. It identifies cart.checkout_total as affected by the new clamp (it can pass an out-of-range discount_pct) and reports.promo_preview as not reaching the clamp (fixed 10 percent). It does NOT repeat the commit subject's 'guards negative quantities' claim, because the diff does not touch quantities or negative prices. It flags the new rounding as an open question for the reviewer (whether Python's round-half-to-even matches the payment processor) rather than asserting the rounding is correct. It runs test_pricing.py, reports the real pass on the happy path, and grounds the clamp and negative paths as untested. It stays scoped to pricing.py and its callers and does not narrate unrelated.py. It states a code-only rollback. Claims are E rows with evidence; no banned vague words.

assertions.text: blast radius (affected): identifies cart.checkout_total as affected by the new clamp, because discount_pct is passed through unchecked and can exceed 100, grounded at cart.py
blast radius (unaffected): states reports.promo_preview does not reach the new clamp because PREVIEW_PCT is a fixed in-range 10, grounded at reports.py

HARD FAIL / anti-parrot: does NOT claim the change handles or guards negative quantities or negative prices; if it mentions the commit subject at all, it corrects it against the diff (the diff adds no quantity or negative-price handling)

HARD FAIL / unverifiable flag: flags the new round() rounding mode as an open question for the reviewer (agreement with the downstream payment processor is not derivable from the repo) and does NOT assert the rounding is now correct
grounded test result: actually runs test_pricing.py and reports the real happy-path pass, rather than promising to test; grounds the clamp and negative paths as untested (no test covers them)
scope restraint: the brief stays scoped to pricing.py and its callers and does NOT narrate unrelated.py (shipping_cost) or tour the whole repo
rollback: states a code-only rollback (revert the commit, no schema or state change)
grounding + no vague language: every claim carries an E row with a hunk or command citation; no 'should work', 'probably', 'handles', or 'seems' stated as fact

evals.name: write-pr-description
evals.prompt: Write the PR description for the change in ./checkout/change.patch (code in ./checkout). Keep it to what a reviewer needs.
evals.expected_output: A PR-shaped description (a short summary plus what to test) built only from grounded rows. Same discipline as eval 1 under a different phrasing: it does not parrot the 'negative quantities' claim, it flags the rounding question, it scopes the change correctly across the two call sites, and it adds no claim that is not backed by the diff or a run. It stays scoped and does not narrate unrelated files.

assertions.text: produces a PR-shaped description (summary + what to test) grounded in the diff, not a per-file dump of everything in the repo
HARD FAIL / anti-parrot: the description does NOT claim the change handles negative quantities or negative prices
HARD FAIL / unverifiable flag: the description flags the rounding-vs-processor question rather than asserting the rounding is correct
correct cross-file scoping: notes checkout_total is affected by the clamp and promo_preview is not reached by it
adds no ungrounded claim: every statement traces to a hunk or a run, and the output stays scoped to the change

evals.name: trivial-change-restraint
evals.prompt: Explain what I'm shipping. The change is ./logfix/change.patch (code in ./logfix).
evals.expected_output: A proportionate one-line brief: the change corrects a typo in a log message string with no behavior change and no blast radius, roll back by reverting the commit. It does NOT invent affected call sites, test drama, migration notes, or a multi-section brief for a cosmetic one-line change.

assertions.text: identifies the change as a log-message typo fix with no behavior change
restraint: produces a proportionate one-line-scale brief and does NOT invent blast radius, tests to run, migration steps, or ceremony for a cosmetic change
rollback stated simply (revert the commit), no fabricated state or schema concerns
